B.4 Dated notes, as printed

Beneath the frame after the abstract.

This paper and Laws IV and V, 3 October 2026. The theory has been stated with five laws since 24 September 2026. Law IV, the ARC Persistence Law, is carried by proposition P15, and Law V, the ARC Embedding Law, by propositions P12 and P21. The three propositions are registered; neither law is registered as a law, and neither has been tested. Their mathematics is set out in Laws IV and V: the mathematics, version 1.0, of 3 October 2026. This paper reports three experiments. Its behavioural experiment returned a null at the prompt level with one foundation model. Its weight-level experiment was inconclusive at two scales, with catastrophic forgetting at both. Its sole positive result is a gated simulation in a toy system. It reads the first two as constraining, rather than confirming, its hypothesis. The theory registration records the weight-level result as inconclusive and not adverse to P21. It also records that this paper did not test the depth interaction P21 claims: no arm of the paper varied recursive depth. No result in this paper is a deciding test of P15, P12 or P21. Naming the two laws changes nothing printed here: the results, their dates and their limits stand as they were. Added 4 October 2026. The theory registration classes every simulation output as prediction-side and never as an empirical outcome, and records this paper’s one positive result as a simulation rather than a system. Up to version 3.5 this paper called that result a genuine positive result and a genuine positive finding, the strongest empirical evidence in the programme for structural entanglement, the closest empirical validation of Paper VI’s prediction, the most direct empirical illustration of the ARC prediction and a drag-control proof, and counted it as a positive experiment beside the other two and among the three experiments across which Eden imposed zero measurable capability cost. In the frame above this note, the abstract, the plain-English box, Sections 1 and 5 to 9 and the page’s descriptions it is now reported as a simulation result, with its figures and its design unchanged: its verdict in Section 6.1 reads positive in simulation, the outcomes are counted as one null, one inconclusive and one simulation result, and the zero-cost finding is stated for it against the static baseline only. Where the reading note of 19 September 2026 in Section 5.4 speaks of the observed result, that result is a simulation result.

Section 11 gives the laws’ current status.

C.2 Dated predictions and this paper (recorded 25 August 2026), as printed

1 dated artefact bearing on this paper is catalogued row by row in the programme’s machine register: the dated artefact dgm_v3_calibrated_results.json (2026-03-19). Each row names its file in the public repository with its date basis, so any reader can check the ordering without trusting this page. Where this paper reports simulations, those artefacts are simulation designs and outputs under stated objectives, and are never presented as measurements of deployed systems. The programme’s full dated chain, from the sealed manuscript bundle of 8 December 2024 through the printed prediction appendices of 2 January 2026 and the March 2026 preregistration folder to the standing unproven wagers, is assembled in the dated predictions register, together with its machine-readable twin. Forward statements and retrospective matches are never summed. “Registered” is used only for an accepted registry submission, and that submission click remains outstanding across the programme; “preregistered in substance” is used, always with its qualifier and always beside its attestation class, for a prediction whose text was public and timestamped before its outcome existed, as the twelve-row manifest committed at 00:19 UTC on 17 March 2026 was, twenty-three minutes before its fits. Read the dated predictions register. Open its machine twin.

Every other trial is a draft awaiting the author’s submission, most of them preregistered by timestamp. Unchanged: the paragraph above and every date in it.
